cohort: 351 women out of 736 eligible women who gave birth at a maternity unit in a medical center in Taiwan
finding: Compared to vaginal delivery, cesarean delivery was associated with a higher prevalence of depressive symptoms at 3 months postpartum and higher pain levels persisting up to 6 months postpartum.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with higher non-localized and abdominal pain, lower perineal pain, higher sexual desire, and lower sexual satisfaction at various time points within the first year postpartum compared to vaginal delivery.
followup_time: 4-6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum
